claims.text: Using machine-learning models trained on high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic data could overcome limited accuracy in determining high-temperature solid and liquid properties.
Using these machine-learning models could improve the availability of high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic-property estimates across a large compositional space.
Using these machine-learning models could improve the efficiency of determining high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing 3-10 principal elements.
The intervention is applicable over 500-2000 K.
Machine-learning models learn patterns and relationships from thermodynamic-property data.
The learned patterns enable accurate prediction across a large compositional space.
The intervention will improve predictions of melting temperature.
The intervention will improve predictions of enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The intervention will improve predictions of volume change upon melting.
The intervention will improve predictions of liquid thermodynamic properties.
Prediction error will be reduced by 20-30% relative to current experimental and computational baselines.
Differential scanning calorimetry and density functional theory represent current experimental and computational baselines.
The machine-learning models may suffer from overfitting or underfitting.
The availability of high-quality training data is limited.
Independent experimental measurements, including differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction, can serve as reference data for the listed thermodynamic properties.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if model predictions deviate from independent reference data by more than 10%.
